question: Controlled: what does the pepM pre-screen cost and change on a dilute full taxon, one taxon, one code version?
method: 2,863 Erwiniaceae genomes, run end-to-end twice on the same commit, identical except pepm_prescreen. GTDB-Tk off in both arms. Params passed in JSON files (run_erwin_screen_{off,on}.json, committed here), never on the CLI: `--pepm_prescreen false` arrives as the string "false", which is truthy in Groovy. bigscape_min_bgc_length=2000 from nextflow.config, confirmed applied in both databases.
why_this_run_exists: It supersedes the uncontrolled Erwiniaceae pair behind the "6.5x" claim. That pair was internally consistent -- both arms realtime x cpus -- but its two sides were different code: the screen-on arm batched antiSMASH and ran RECOVER_ORFS, the screen-off arm did neither, and GTDB-Tk differed. Controlling that moves 6.47x -> 5.49x on the same basis; reporting on realtime x %cpu moves it further to 5.14x.
controls_verified: both arms aggregated on the same basis (realtime x %cpu) from the committed traces
antiSMASH task granularity identical (50 genomes per task, both arms) -- held fixed as good practice, though it is not what drove the old discrepancy
FETCH_RENAME_SCREEN: 115 tasks in both arms, same genomes fetched
pepm_prescreen is the only differing parameter

the_screens_own_cost.how_measured: FETCH_RENAME_SCREEN is 83.1 CPU-min with the screen on against 14.3 with it off. The screen is no longer a separately timed stage -- a rejected genome is deleted before its output is declared, so it never reaches publishDir -- so its cost is the arm-to-arm delta of the fused process. Both arms run 115 such tasks over the same genomes, so the delta is the screening work and nothing else.
the_screens_own_cost.supersedes: 91.3 CPU-min, which was a PEPM_PRESCREEN stage total from the older pair AND on the other accounting basis (realtime x cpus). On realtime x cpus the screen here costs 8.6 CPU-min, not 68.8 -- the two numbers are not comparable.

recover_orfs_also_shrinks: 257.4 -> 14.0 CPU-min (18x). RECOVER_ORFS only sees genomes that passed the screen, so this is a real downstream saving -- but it is NOT the screen acting on antiSMASH, which is why the headline ratio is quoted on antiSMASH CPU alone.
caveats: antiSMASH CPU-minutes are the comparable column. Whole-pipeline totals fold in RECOVER_ORFS, whose asymmetry is intrinsic to screening rather than a separate effect.
2,863 genomes, not the 2,771 of the 2026-09 runs: the NCBI download grew. Counts are therefore not directly comparable to the older Erwiniaceae records.

The traces here were written by a -resume, which rewrites pipeline_trace.tsv in place. Nearly every row is CACHED and carries the realtime of the session that actually ran it, so any re-analysis must sum CACHED as well as COMPLETED.
cached_realtimes_cross_checked: These CPU sums come from CACHED trace rows, so they rest on CACHED carrying the realtime of the session that actually ran each task. Checked independently against .nextflow/history, which the launcher writes separately from the trace observer: the screen-off original (session 8f15d50e, 2026-10-31 17:35) ran 314.2 min wall for 2,287.2 CPU-min = 7.28 mean parallelism, the screen-on original (session 90f5f78d, 16:23) 72.5 min wall for 497.7 CPU-min = 6.87, on a 16-core box. Two runs of very different length and composition agreeing on ~7 is not what stale, zeroed, or resume-length (17-22 s) realtimes would produce. The Nextflow cache DB could not be queried directly -- no JVM is installed outside the pipeline's conda envs.
cpu_accounting_basis: realtime x %cpu (ACTUAL CPU utilisation). The superseded pepm_prescreen/summary.json uses realtime x cpus (ALLOCATED cores) instead, so no figure here may be compared with a figure there. On realtime x cpus this run is ANTISMASH 3,450.8 -> 629.1 CPU-min, 5.49x.
a_retracted_explanation: An earlier version of this file blamed antiSMASH task granularity (2,760 one-genome tasks vs 7 batched). That is WRONG: modules/analysis/antismash.nf loops "for GENOME in ${genomes}" and invokes antiSMASH once per genome even inside a batched task, so batching amortises Nextflow task overhead only. Like-for-like, antiSMASH per-genome cost barely moved between the two eras: 43.3 -> 41.6 CPU-s/genome on realtime x %cpu, 80.1 -> 72.3 on realtime x cpus. The apparent "80.4 -> 41.6" collapse was entirely the unit mismatch above.

populations_for_projection.why: Every stage prices against a DIFFERENT population, and conflating two of them is how the GTDB-Tk row came to be overstated by 15%. Counted from main_analysis_results/Erwiniaceae/region_counts.tsv in both arms.
populations_for_projection.identical_in_both_arms: 308 screened is the screen-on arm's input; BGC-positive (300) and regions (335) are identical in BOTH arms, which is the detection-neutrality result.
